request.recipient: Intersect, via the listed 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address.
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Intersect governance coordination, technical stewardship, incident response, release coordination, and critical process management for June 2026 to June 2027.

claims.claim: Intersect says this proposal funds its core operating model for June 2026 to June 2027, including governance coordination, technical stewardship, incident response, release coordination, and critical unowned processes.

The proposal requests 25,400,000 ADA, allocated as 6,000,000 ADA for operations and ecosystem coordination, 18,800,000 ADA for technical stewardship and incident response, and 600,000 ADA for critical process management.
Intersect states its overall ask has decreased from $7.875M last year to $6.35M while preserving functions it considers critical to Cardano continuity and maturity.
Intersect claims it has coordinated two network upgrades, is preparing for a third, and led ecosystem coordination during the November 2025 chain partition incident.

The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and provides references to voting documentation, audited results, and an audit report.
The proposal states the requested amount does not, at submission, breach the applicable 350M ADA Net Change Limit for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 and links to the relevant governance action.
The proposal says independent audits and assurance will be provided by Appold and may include deliverable verification, control testing, spend validation, and milestone evidence assessment.
Intersect discloses that it and its committees received 22,385,000 ADA in Cardano Treasury funding through listed governance actions within the past 24 months.

Intersect says treasury funds will be administered through Sundae Labs smart contract tooling with specified TRSC and PSSC addresses, permission thresholds, an external Oversight Committee, and a public dashboard.
The proposal claims Intersect currently supports thousands of participants across members, committees, and working groups through its Member-Based Organization structure.

summary: The document requests 25,400,000 ADA for Intersect’s 2026-2027 governance coordination and technical stewardship work, gives a high-level work-package budget, cites Hydra voting and smart-contract references, discloses prior treasury funding, and describes oversight mechanisms, but it does not provide a complete detailed budget, feasibility analysis, risk analysis, alternatives analysis, or failure-mode analysis in the supplied text.
